content.text:
USER: Take a look at this project. It needs to be 100% hardened and foolproof. I can't have AI making bad decision and causing a massive failure that ends up costing my company a lot of money because we didn't do our job of title search and approval properly.
ASSISTANT (message): I'll take a thorough look at the project structure first to understand what we're working with.

content.thinking:
The user just expressed a high‑level concern about hardening the project and preventing any AI‑driven mistakes in title search and approval. I have no concrete details yet about the repository contents, so the first thing I need to do is explore the file system to see what code, documentation, or configuration files are present. Without that visibility I can't assess any security gaps, locate the title search logic, or identify where approvals are handled.

I could ask the user for more specifics, but that would delay the analysis and the user likely expects me to start inspecting the project immediately. The safest, most systematic approach is to list all files and directories at the root of the workspace. Using the `Glob` tool with a wildcard pattern will give me a complete inventory of everything in the current directory tree. This will let me decide which files to open next (e.g., look for README, security policies, source code directories, test suites, CI configs, etc.) and will form the basis for any hardening recommendations.

There are no arguments needed beyond the pattern; `"*"` will match every file and folder recursively. I’ll invoke the Glob tool with that pattern now to get the project layout.
